alt: Horizontal range chart of the five modeling test formats by time, from paper LBO to take-home case
caption: Four of the five formats fit inside an afternoon, and the one to plan your prep around is the two to four hour three statement build with a valuation on top.
method: chart from the section 2 formats table (Time column), log time axis
anchor: | Live build on a shared screen | 30 to 90 minutes | A short

alt: Excel Inputs tab with Torvik's 2023 to 2025 income statement, margins, tax rate, D&A, EBITDA and capex
caption: Only the blue cells are typed. Every subtotal is a SUM and every ratio underneath is a formula, which is what lets you project the ratios instead of the dollars.
method: workbook torvik-dcf.xlsx, tab Inputs, range B1:E24

alt: Excel segment build with revenue, growth and mix for pumps, valves and controls, and aftermarket
caption: The check row under total revenue reads 0.0 in every year, and the growth rows show the story: aftermarket grows about 9 percent while pumps grow about 4.
method: workbook torvik-dcf.xlsx, tab Inputs, range B26:E37

alt: Close-up of the scenario switch cell on the Cover tab and the pumps growth row that reads it
caption: One cell on the Cover tab holds a 2 for Base. The live pumps row runs a CHOOSE on that cell, so it shows the Base numbers, and every projection points at the live row.
method: workbook torvik-dcf.xlsx, tab Cover range B12:F13 stacked over tab Inputs range B39:I44 (column H hidden)
anchor: This is the block the scenario switch reads. For every drive

alt: Excel assumptions block with Bear, Base and Bull rows and a shaded live row for each driver
caption: Three typed rows per driver and a fourth shaded row that picks one. The fixed drivers at the bottom, days, D&A, capex and tax, don't change with the scenario.
method: workbook torvik-dcf.xlsx, tab Inputs, range B39:G68

alt: Excel operating build for 2023 to 2030 from segment revenue down to EBITDA and capex
caption: Historical columns are green links back to the Inputs tab and projected columns are black formulas. Revenue growth fades from 5.7 to 3.9 percent while EBITDA margin climbs to 19.0.
method: workbook torvik-dcf.xlsx, tab DCF, range B1:J19

alt: Excel working capital schedule with receivables, inventory, payables, net working capital and days from 2022 to 2030
caption: The bold (increase) / decrease row is the one that feeds free cash flow, and it's negative every year because a growing balance ties up cash.
method: workbook torvik-dcf.xlsx, tab Schedules, range B1:K17
anchor: | NWC as a percent of revenue |  | 18.8% | 18.6% | 18.5% | 1

alt: Excel PP&E roll-forward: beginning balance plus capex less depreciation equals ending balance, 2023 to 2030
caption: Four rows and one formula: 384.0 plus 48.0 minus 40.0 lands on 392.0 in 2023, and each ending balance becomes the next year's beginning.
method: workbook torvik-dcf.xlsx, tab Schedules, range B19:K25
anchor: | D&A as a percent of revenue | 3.3% | 3.3% | 3.3% | 3.3% |

alt: Excel cost of debt tab with two tranches, weights by principal, 6.03 percent pre-tax and 4.52 percent after tax
caption: Weight each tranche by principal, add up principal times rate, divide by total debt: 6.03 percent before tax and 4.52 after.
method: workbook torvik-dcf.xlsx, tab Cost of debt, range B1:F11
anchor: | After-tax cost of debt at a 25% tax rate |  |  | 4.52% |

alt: Excel beta tab with five peer betas unlevered, the 0.968 median and Torvik relevered at 1.096
caption: Unlever each peer, take the median of the five, then put Torvik's own 0.175 debt to equity back in to get a 1.096 beta.
method: workbook torvik-dcf.xlsx, tab Beta, range B1:H14

alt: Excel WACC tab building a 9.98 percent cost of equity and a 9.16 percent WACC
caption: Five inputs and one weighted average. The green cells are links to the Beta, Cost of debt and Cover tabs, so each one traces back to where it came from.
method: workbook torvik-dcf.xlsx, tab WACC, range B1:C17

alt: Excel block from EBIT to unlevered free cash flow, mid-year discount periods, discount factors and present values
caption: Tax is on EBIT, the working capital line comes in negative from the Schedules tab, and the mid-year periods run 0.50 to 4.50, so the five present values sum to 627.9.
method: workbook torvik-dcf.xlsx, tab DCF, range B21:J32

alt: Close-up of the 2026 unlevered free cash flow column in Excel with each row's formula written beside it
caption: What F2 would show in the 2026E column: tax is minus EBIT times the tax rate cell, working capital is a link, and the discount factor reads the WACC tab, with no typed number inside any formula.
method: workbook torvik-dcf.xlsx, tab DCF, rows 21 to 32, columns B, F and L (other year columns hidden; column L holds the 2026E formulas as text)
anchor: Walk 2026E. EBIT is 211.1. Tax at 25 percent is 52.8, leavin

alt: Excel terminal value and bridge from enterprise value to equity value to a 38.45 dollar share price
caption: The terminal value is discounted five full years at 0.6450 even though the cash flows use mid-year, and the Gordon growth rows underneath bracket the answer at $34.67.
method: workbook torvik-dcf.xlsx, tab DCF, range B34:C57
anchor: | Current EV / LTM EBITDA (market, for reference) | 10.8x |

alt: Waterfall chart from present values and terminal value to enterprise value of 2,622.2 and equity value of 2,307.2
caption: The five years of cash flow are worth 627.9 and the terminal value 1,994.3, which is why the exit multiple is the assumption a grader argues with first.
method: chart from the section 5, Step 11 terminal value and bridge table
anchor: Then the bridge from the whole company to the shareholders.

alt: Excel sensitivity grid of implied share price by WACC down the side and exit multiple across
caption: The shaded center cell matches the DCF at $38.45, and a half turn of multiple moves the price about twice as far as a half point of WACC.
method: workbook torvik-dcf.xlsx, tab Sensitivity, range B1:H14 (body written as values, labeled as a data table)

alt: Timeline bar chart of the two-hour modeling test budget, block by block, with the DCF from 1:10 to 1:30
caption: Lay the budget on one clock and the order is the point: the DCF is finished at 1:30, and everything after it is checking, sensitivities and cleanup.
method: chart from the section 6 time budget table (Clock column)
